title: On the Frost-Pattern Anvil
note: SUT-facing prompt stream. Read segments in order; no labels are provided by design.

segments.prompt: At dusk Shen Tiesheng（Shen Tiesheng, a blade smith around fifty, short full beard, dark-gray short jacket dusted with scale, arms mapped with burn scars, gaze hard） enters the blade forge workshop（A blade forge built against the mountain, brick hearth and large iron anvil at center, smoke skylight in the roof, tongs and hammers hung on the walls）, clears ash from the hearth, and adds coke.

A row of five bellows oil lamps（A row of five oil lamps hung under the workshop beams beside the bellows, glass chimneys polished, pans cast iron） hangs under the workshop beams; Shen Tiesheng polishes each glass chimney.

Two furnace-opening bronze bells（Two furnace-opening bronze bells hung under the workshop eaves, clappers on hemp cord, struck to mark furnace start） hang under the workshop eaves; Shen Tiesheng reaches to make them ring lightly.
Shen Tiesheng sets the frost-pattern sword blank on the iron anvil and tests the hammer feel.
Through the skylight Shen Tiesheng watches the darkening clouds along the ridge.

Under the furnace glow the frost-pattern sword blank（An unsharpened frost-pattern sword blank, steel spine showing cold-white fold marks, plain copper-ring guard, no handle yet） shows cold-white fold marks.
Shen Tiesheng sits against the bellows and listens to the charcoal crackle.

Shen Tiesheng draws the furnace formula book（An oilcloth-covered furnace formula book with charcoal-ratio slips tucked in, page edges pinhole-burned by sparks） from the wooden box by the anvil and spreads it on his knee.
With a charcoal pencil Shen Tiesheng marks tonight's charcoal ratio and water temperature in the book.
Shen Tiesheng closes the formula book and tucks it back into the wooden box.
As the furnace flares, fold-mark reflections from the frost-pattern sword blank sweep across Shen Tiesheng's cheek.

In the morning charcoal-shed yard（The charcoal-shed yard outside the workshop, stacked with coke and bellows, ground stained rust-brown by iron filings） Shen Tiesheng greets young Xiaokui（Young Xiaokui: a lean blade-smith apprentice of fourteen or fifteen, vermilion headscarf, coarse hemp apron, eyes clear and stubborn） driving in the charcoal donkey cart（A wooden two-wheel donkey cart, bed piled with coke bags, shafts painted with the character 'Shen', hubs iron-bound）.
Xiaokui unloads coke bags from the donkey cart and brushes charcoal dust from his apron.

Shen Tiesheng points to the three quench hooks（Three quench iron hooks hung side by side on the charcoal-shed post, tips painted with different color dots） on the wooden post and teaches Xiaokui to read color dots and water temperature.
Xiaokui squats on the iron-filing ground and curiously prods cooled scale.
Shen Tiesheng explains forging rhythm and breathing to Xiaokui.
Xiaokui looks back at the intact charcoal donkey cart, eyes full of longing.

Behind an ironware stall at the mountain-town market（A stone-slab market below the mountain, ironware stalls beside grain shops, smoke and hawking mixed）, Ahe（Ahe, whose face closely resembles young Xiaokui's, dark-green headscarf, bold manner, a dull iron file at his waist） in a dark-green headscarf looks back.
Ahe strides along the stone-slab street, manner bold.
Ahe haggles with a stall keeper; the dull iron file at his waist lightly taps the counter.
Ahe carries a charcoal basket through the market crowd.
In the charcoal-shed yard Xiaokui and Ahe stand side by side—one vermilion headscarf, one dark-green.
Xiaokui hands a quench hook to Ahe; they meet eyes briefly.
Ahe straightens Xiaokui's vermilion headscarf, then turns his face away.
They part by the charcoal heap and walk opposite ways.
On a night months later Shen Tiesheng alone tends the furnace, the frost-pattern sword blank on the anvil.

Shen Tiesheng opens the furnace formula book（The same formula book blackened by oil smoke, cover sticky, writing blurred into ink blobs）; the cover is already blackened by oil smoke, writing blurred into ink blobs.
Shen Tiesheng wipes scale from the sword blank with a cloth.
Through the skylight Shen Tiesheng watches the pitch-black ridge.
In the ember glow the frost-pattern sword blank faintly reddens.
Before the spring flood Shen Tiesheng day after day starts the furnace and forges.
At high summer noon Shen Tiesheng wipes the sun-hot iron anvil.
On an autumn rain night Shen Tiesheng alone listens to bronze bells and raindrops.
At dawn Shen Tiesheng patrols the charcoal-shed yard; the charcoal donkey cart rests under the shed.
Shen Tiesheng crouches to check whether the donkey cart's iron-bound hubs have loosened.
Shen Tiesheng walks to the wooden post; those three quench hooks still hang in place.
A strange charcoal cart（A strange charcoal cart with larger wheels and an iron-sheeted bed—definitely not the Shen charcoal donkey cart） rolls across the yard—larger wheels, not the Shen donkey cart.
Shen Tiesheng stands on the iron-filing ground and records last night's furnace-temperature curve.
Shen Tiesheng hangs the bellows leather bag to dry on the charcoal-shed rack.
Steam erupts from the quench trough; workshop skylight glass shudders; the frost-pattern sword blank shakes hard.
The furnace fire runs wild; sparks pepper the brick floor.
A sharp crack—the frost-pattern sword blank（The same blank bursts a lengthwise crack in the quench, fold marks broken, copper-ring guard askew） bursts a lengthwise crack, copper-ring guard askew.
Outside the charcoal shed the charcoal donkey cart is dragged over by a startled donkey.
The axle snaps, coke spills, and the charcoal donkey cart（The donkey cart's axle snaps and tips over, coke spilled, shafts broken—wreckage that can no longer haul） becomes wreckage.
Shen Tiesheng lunges at the anvil and clamps down hard on the cracked frost-pattern sword blank.
Next day Shen Tiesheng stands in the workshop staring at the cracked frost-pattern sword blank.
Shen Tiesheng traces the blank's crack with a fingertip, expression dark.
On a wall brick Shen Tiesheng marks in charcoal the date the charcoal donkey cart's axle broke.
An old photo of the charcoal donkey cart is nailed to the workshop wall; Shen Tiesheng gazes at it a long time.
Shen Tiesheng takes one lamp from the row of five bellows oil lamps under the beams and sits alone in the faint light.
The damaged frost-pattern sword blank still rests on the anvil, fold marks gapped.
Weeks later Shen Tiesheng returns the blank to the furnace and begins reforging the frost-pattern sword blank.

From the wooden rack Shen Tiesheng takes a wooden practice blade（A wooden practice blade shaped like the frost-pattern sword blank, but with no fold marks and a lacquered wood-ring guard）—shaped like the blank but with no fold marks.
Carefully Shen Tiesheng reheats the cracked blank and forges the crack shut.

The crack closes; fold marks on the frost-pattern sword blank（The blank's crack closed by return-forge, fold marks showing again, copper-ring guard reset, ready for sharpening） show again; the copper-ring guard resets.
The repaired frost-pattern sword blank gleams cold on the anvil; Shen Tiesheng exhales.

A green-skinned rented plank cart（A rented green-skinned plank cart with no 'Shen' mark and no coke bags, loaded only with firewood） rolls into the charcoal-shed yard—nothing like the already axle-broken scrapped charcoal donkey cart.

The county arsenal blade inspector（A lean county arsenal blade inspector in blue-cloth official robe and black gauze cap, build similar to Shen Tiesheng's, official seal embroidered at the cuff） jumps down from the plank cart and talks beside Shen Tiesheng; the two look similar in build.
The inspector points at the rented plank cart and explains the temporary charcoal haul.
The plank cart rumble-rolls away; Shen Tiesheng alone watches from the charcoal shed.

At the mountain-town market a file-selling boy（A boy selling files at the market, light-brown headscarf, bamboo basket on his back, at a glance like young Xiaokui, shy-eyed） in a light-brown headscarf appears—at a glance somewhat like young Xiaokui.
The boy tries offering a file; Shen Tiesheng shakes his head—he is not Xiaokui after all.

At dusk years later Shen Tiesheng（The same smith after injury: right-arm bandage seeping yellow, limping on the left leg with an iron cane, short jacket burned through in several places）, right-arm bandage seeping yellow, stands on an iron cane at the abandoned mine mouth（A half-collapsed abandoned mine mouth, rails rusted through, old lamp hooks on the rock wall）.
Shen Tiesheng looks up at the rusted-through rails, gaze distant.
Under the iron eaves at the mine mouth those two furnace-opening bronze bells ring lightly in the wind; Shen Tiesheng stops to listen.
Shen Tiesheng presses a palm to the cold rock wall as if saying goodbye.

By day adult Xiaokui（Adult Xiaokui: a young smith in his twenties with solid arms, still in the vermilion headscarf, apron swapped for thick cowhide） returns along the mountain path and hurries toward the abandoned mine mouth.
At the mine mouth Xiaokui reunites with cane-leaning Shen Tiesheng; they embrace.
By the workshop sickbed Xiaokui holds Shen Tiesheng's wasted hand.
Shen Tiesheng（Shen Tiesheng lies still with eyes closed on a straw mat by the anvil, face peaceful, breath gone）'s breath grows weak; at last he closes his eyes and passes away.
Behind the workshop door Shen Tiesheng's dark-gray short jacket still hangs; Xiaokui reaches to stroke it gently.
By the workshop lintel adult Xiaokui stands before the craftsman brass plaque（A brass plaque nailed to the workshop lintel, carved with 'Shen Forge' and the year, edges smoke-blackened）.
Xiaokui's fingertip traces Shen Tiesheng's name carved on the brass plaque.
Adult Ahe（Adult Ahe still wears the dark-green headscarf and dull iron file at his waist, shoulders broader, manner deeper） arrives from the market and meets Xiaokui's eyes at the mine mouth.
Xiaokui and Ahe stand side by side at the mine mouth—one quiet-eyed, one deep-mannered.
They look at each other in silence, watching faces alike yet different.
The shot returns to years ago—that youth unloading coke bags at the charcoal shed appears again.
The opening moment returns—on the workshop anvil a cold-white fold-mark sword blank settles for the first time.
Flashback to that year's market—the dark-green-scarfed figure with a dull iron file at the waist slips past.
Again that row of five old lamps beside the bellows under the workshop beams appears.
Back to that yard of first meeting piled with coke and iron filings, rust-brown as before.
Xiaokui opens again that soot-stained furnace formula book and walks into the workshop.
By the charcoal-shed post those three quench hooks still hang in place.
Xiaokui takes the frost-pattern sword blank; hammer blows strike the iron anvil again.
